claim: For a stationary finite-alphabet process with a supplied absolute-regularity envelope beta, a predictor q selected from the training prefix of one raw trajectory and satisfying q(v|c)>=xi has a valid high-probability upper certificate for stationary-context conditional KL over any fixed L-symbol context and H-symbol future block, using a temporally separated validation segment from that same trajectory.

interface.observed: one stationary raw path Y_1:T over a finite alphabet
interface.additional_promise: known beta-mixing envelope beta(s); finite context length L, forecast horizon H, predictor floor xi

quantifiers: For every stationary process on alphabet size a, L,H>=1, delta in (0,1), training-selected normalized q with q(v|c)>=xi, and validation block schedule described in RESULT.txt, with probability >=1-delta-M beta(g+1), R(q)<=min{ln(1/xi), Rhat(q)+r ln(1/xi)+2 omega_K^+(r)}.
finite_diagnostic: work/programmes/acquisition_learning/cycle3/lead_beta_certificate/verify_certificate.py checks 11,025 rational binary-context/binary-future instances; it is not proof validation.
cost: K=a^(L+H); M>=((K+1)ln2+ln(1/delta))/(2r^2) yields TV radius r; raw symbols T>=n+g+M(L+H)+(M-1)g; mixing failure M beta(g+1); O(K log M) count storage; certified logarithm precision must be added for bit-level certification.
baseline: A learner retaining all raw symbols can replay the same selection/certificate; no trajectory-sample advantage is claimed.
failure_boundary: Without a known mixing envelope the certificate confidence is unbounded; as L or H grows the alphabet factor is exponential; the certificate is stationary-context averaged and does not cover all histories or infinite-future KL.
